title: Color Equivariant Convolutional Networks

en.text: Color is one of the most reliable cues a convolutional network can lean on. A ripe tomato is red, a school bus is yellow, a particular flower is a characteristic purple-blue. Networks pick up on this quickly, and most of the time it helps. But the same reliance becomes a liability the moment the colors at test time drift away from the colors seen during training. A model that learned cars mostly from red and silver examples can stumble on a blue one, even though the shape is unmistakable.

The usual defense against this is color invariance: convert to grayscale, or drown the network in aggressive color-jitter augmentation until it stops caring about hue. That does buy robustness, but at a real cost. Grayscale simply deletes a genuinely useful signal, and heavy augmentation blurs the very color distinctions that separate one class from another. You end up robust to color precisely by refusing to use it.

A NeurIPS 2023 paper from the Computer Vision Lab at Delft University of Technology proposes a different bargain. Instead of choosing between exploiting color and being robust to color changes, it treats a hue shift the way earlier work treated a rotation or a flip: as a symmetry the network should respect by construction. The building block that does this is the Color Equivariant Convolution (CEConv), and it drops into a standard ResNet with no architectural surgery.

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea. A hue transform T_g turns flower A into flower B. A vanilla CNN maps the two into unrelated predictions, so a class it learned in one color may be unrecognizable in another. A Color Equivariant CNN (CECNN) instead maps them to representations related by a predictable permutation T'_g, so shape knowledge learned for one color transfers to the others.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19368
Code: https://github.com/Attila94/CEConv
The problem: color helps, until the colors change

Real-world appearance has a long tail. For almost any object category, some colors are common in the training set and others are rare or entirely absent, and no realistic dataset can cover every variation. Because a standard CNN treats each color as its own visual pattern, the shape knowledge it builds for a well-represented color does not automatically carry over to an underrepresented one. The rare colors are exactly the ones that get misclassified, and collecting a perfectly color-balanced dataset is not a practical option.

The paper first makes the tension concrete: CNNs clearly benefit from color, yet they are not robust to color-based distribution shifts. Grayscale models and color augmentation restore robustness, but they do so by discarding the discriminative color information that helps in the first place. The goal is to keep color and generalize across it at the same time, so that a shape learned in one part of the spectrum is available everywhere.
The idea: a hue shift is a rotation in RGB space

Group equivariant convolutions taught networks to share parameters across geometric transformations such as rotations and reflections, which made them far more data efficient for those symmetries. Photometric transformations like hue shifts had been left out, even though studies of trained CNNs show that early layers learn strongly color-selective filters. Color, in other words, is a natural axis along which to demand equivariance.

The key observation is geometric. A hue shift in HSV space corresponds, in RGB space, to a rotation around the gray diagonal that runs from black to white, the [1,1,1] axis. The authors formalize the set of discrete hue shifts as the group H_n of n rotations by 360/n degrees about that diagonal. A Color Equivariant Convolution then correlates the input not with a single filter but with a set of hue-rotated copies of it, producing a feature map that carries an extra dimension indexing which hue rotation each response came from.

For the input layer this means rotating each filter by the hue matrix H_n(k); for hidden layers the filter copies are cyclically permuted across the color dimension, so equivariance is preserved all the way through the network. Concretely, the response at spatial location x and hue index k is:
[f * psi^i](x, k) = sum over y in Z^2, sum over c = 1..C^l  of  f_c(y) . H_n(k) psi_c^i(y - x), where the sum runs over spatial positions y and input channels c.

The extra color dimension multiplies the number of feature maps, so the authors keep the cost in check by decomposing each filter into a spatial and a pointwise component, which limits the growth in operations and parameters to a small factor of the number of hue rotations. They also offer hybrid variants that apply CEConvs only in the early, most color-selective ResNet stages and then pool over the color dimension, introducing color invariance later in the network while controlling capacity.
Robustness without a clean-accuracy tax

The headline result is that color equivariance buys robustness for free on clean data. On the original, unshifted test sets, a CE-ResNet performs on par with its vanilla ResNet counterpart. The difference only shows up when the test images are re-rendered under a gradual hue shift sweeping from -180 to 180 degrees, and accuracy is averaged across the whole range. There the gap opens dramatically.

Figure 2 tells the story for Flowers-102. Read the vanilla CNN (blue) first: it forms a single sharp peak at 0 degrees, right where the training colors sit, and collapses toward a few percent as soon as the hue moves away. The color equivariant model (orange) instead shows three peaks, at -120, 0, and 120 degrees, because its discrete hue symmetry lets it recognize the same flower after each of those rotations. Adding color-jitter augmentation on top (dashed orange) flattens the curve into consistently high accuracy across every hue.

en.caption: Figure 2. Test accuracy on Flowers-102 as a function of a test-time hue shift. The vanilla CNN (blue) peaks only near the training colors and collapses elsewhere; the color equivariant CE-CNN (orange) recovers accuracy at each discrete hue rotation, and with color augmentation (dashed) it stays high across the entire hue range.

en.text: Averaged over the full hue sweep, Flowers-102 accuracy climbs from 13.41% for the baseline to 33.33% for the equivariant model, roughly 2.5 times better, and similar gains appear on CIFAR-100 and Stanford Cars. Crucially, these robustness gains do not come at the expense of clean accuracy, and they stack with color augmentation rather than competing with it.
A controlled stress test: long-tailed ColorMNIST

To isolate the mechanism, the authors build a synthetic benchmark, long-tailed ColorMNIST, where digits must be classified by both shape and color and the classes are strongly imbalanced. Because color equivariance shares a shape template across the whole color spectrum, a network can learn a digit's shape from the common colors and still recognize it in the rare ones, which is precisely where a vanilla network runs out of examples.

en.caption: Figure 3. Per-class test accuracy on long-tailed ColorMNIST, with the gray bars showing class frequency. The color equivariant CECNN (green) holds high accuracy even for the rare classes on the right, while the vanilla Z2CNN (blue) and its grayscale variant (orange) fall off sharply as classes become infrequent.

en.text: The effect is large. Averaged over all classes, the color equivariant network reaches 91.35% against the vanilla network's 71.59%, a gain of 19.76 points, and the improvement is concentrated exactly on the rarest classes that parameter sharing is meant to rescue. The controlled setting confirms what the natural-image benchmarks suggest: sharing shape across colors is what turns rare-color examples from failures into successes.

en.caption: Table 1. Average test accuracy (%) over the full test-time hue-shift sweep (-180 to 180 degrees). Color equivariant ResNets are far more robust than vanilla baselines, while matching them on the original, unshifted test sets.

en.text: When does color equivariance help?

Color equivariance is not a universal win, and the paper is candid about when it pays off. Using a color-selectivity measure that quantifies how much a dataset's neurons respond to color, the authors relate the benefit of equivariance both to how color-selective a dataset is and to how deep into the network its equivariant stages are allowed to reach.

en.caption: Figure 4. Accuracy improvement of color equivariant over vanilla models as color equivariance is embedded up to a given ResNet stage, without (left) and with (right) color-jitter augmentation. Flowers-102, whose neurons are highly color-selective (0.70), benefits steadily as equivariance reaches later stages; less color-selective datasets see little or no gain.

en.text: The pattern is clear: a highly color-selective dataset like Flowers-102 (color selectivity 0.70) benefits from color equivariance up to the later stages of the network, while datasets whose neurons care less about color see little change. Two further ablations round out the design. Increasing the number of discrete hue rotations improves test-time robustness, at a slight capacity cost because channels must shrink to keep the parameter count fixed. And group coset pooling turns out to be the mechanism that yields hue invariance; remove it and the network behaves like a regular one.
What the shared filters actually learn

Because equivariance is built into the architecture rather than learned from data, the internal filters have an interpretable structure. Visualizing the neuron features of a CE-ResNet18 trained on Flowers-102 shows that each rotation of a shared filter responds to the same shape rendered in a different color, which is the parameter sharing made visible.

en.caption: Figure 5. Neuron-feature visualizations with top activating patches at four stages of a CE-ResNet18 trained on Flowers-102. Within each block, the rows are different hue rotations of the same shared filter, and each row fires on the same shape in a different color, exactly as color equivariance predicts.

en.text: Takeaways and limits

The lasting message is that color deserves the same equivariance treatment that translation and rotation have long enjoyed. By sharing shape features across the color spectrum while keeping color in a dedicated dimension of the feature map, Color Equivariant Convolutions let a network exploit color and stay robust to color shifts at once, rather than trading one for the other. The block plugs into existing architectures like ResNet, complements color augmentation, and delivers its largest gains precisely on the color-selective datasets and underrepresented colors where it is designed to help.

The honest boundary is that the benefit is conditional. On datasets whose neurons are not especially color-selective, equivariance adds parameters without buying much, and the extra color dimension carries a compute overhead that the filter decomposition reduces but does not erase. Used where color genuinely matters, though, CEConvs offer a clean, practical route to color-robust recognition, and a reminder that a symmetry worth having is usually worth building in.

For practitioners, part of the appeal is that none of this asks for a new architecture or a new training recipe. A CEConv is a drop-in replacement for a standard convolution, the reference implementation is public, and the hybrid variants let you trade the depth of color equivariance against your compute budget. When a task leans on color and the data cannot cover every appearance, it is a cheap symmetry to try before reaching for heavier invariance machinery.

zh.text: 颜色是卷积神经网络最容易利用的线索之一：成熟的番茄是红的，校车是黄的，某种花有着独特的紫蓝色。网络很快就会学到这些规律，多数时候这也确实有帮助。但一旦测试时遇到的颜色与训练时不同，这种依赖就变成了软肋。一个主要从红色、银色样本里学到汽车的模型，看到一辆蓝色汽车时可能就认不出来了，哪怕形状一目了然。
对付这个问题的常规做法是追求颜色不变性（color invariance）：把图像转成灰度，或者用大量 color-jitter（颜色抖动）增强，直到网络不再在意色调。这样确实能换来鲁棒性，但代价很实在。灰度直接删掉了一个本来有用的信号，而强增强又会抹平区分类别所依赖的颜色差异。结果是，你恰恰通过拒绝使用颜色来获得对颜色的鲁棒性。

代尔夫特理工大学（TU Delft）计算机视觉实验室发表于 NeurIPS 2023 的一篇论文提出了另一种取舍。与其在「利用颜色」和「对颜色变化鲁棒」之间二选一，不如把一次色调偏移当作此前工作处理旋转或翻转那样的对象：把它视为网络理应在结构上遵守的一种对称性。承担这一职责的构件就是 Color Equivariant Convolution（CEConv，颜色等变卷积），它无需改动架构，就能作为标准模块直接嵌入 ResNet 这类现有骨干网络。

zh.caption: 图 1 核心思想。色调变换 T_g 把花 A 变成花 B。普通 CNN 会把两者映射到彼此无关的预测上，于是在一种颜色下学到的类别，换个颜色就可能认不出来。颜色等变网络（CECNN）则把它们映射到由一个可预测的置换 T'_g 相联系的表示上，因此为某种颜色学到的形状知识可以迁移到其他颜色。

zh.text: 论文地址：https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19368
代码地址：https://github.com/Attila94/CEConv
问题：颜色有用，直到颜色变了
真实世界的外观有一条长尾。对几乎任何一个物体类别来说，训练集中总有些颜色常见、另一些颜色罕见甚至完全缺席，任何现实数据集都无法覆盖全部变化。由于标准 CNN 把每一种颜色都当作独立的视觉模式，它为某种充分出现的颜色所建立的形状知识，并不会自动迁移到出现不足的颜色上。恰恰是那些罕见颜色最容易被错分，而收集一个颜色完全均衡的数据集在实践中并不可行。
论文首先把这层张力讲清楚：CNN 明显能从颜色中获益，却对基于颜色的分布偏移并不鲁棒。灰度模型和颜色增强能恢复鲁棒性，但代价是丢弃了原本有用的判别性颜色信息。目标是既保留颜色、又能跨颜色泛化，让在色谱某一段学到的形状，在整个色谱上都能用得上。
思路：色调偏移就是 RGB 空间里的一次旋转
群等变卷积（group equivariant convolution）教会网络在旋转、反射等几何变换间共享参数，从而在这些对称性上大幅提升数据效率。而像色调偏移这样的光度变换却一直被搁置，尽管对已训练 CNN 的研究表明，早期层会学到高度颜色选择性的滤波器。换句话说，颜色本身就是一个天然适合施加等变性的坐标轴。
关键的观察是几何性的。HSV 空间中的一次色调偏移，对应到 RGB 空间就是绕着从黑到白的灰度对角线（即 [1,1,1] 轴）的一次旋转。作者把离散色调偏移的集合形式化为群 H_n，即绕该对角线做 n 次、每次 360/n 度旋转所构成的群。颜色等变卷积于是不再只用单个滤波器与输入做相关，而是用一组经过色调旋转的滤波器副本，产生的特征图会多出一个维度，用来标记每个响应来自哪一次色调旋转。
对于输入层，这意味着用色调矩阵 H_n(k) 旋转每个滤波器；对于隐藏层，滤波器副本沿颜色维度做循环置换，从而让等变性在整个网络中一直保持。具体地，空间位置 x、色调索引 k 处的响应为：
[f * psi^i](x, k) = sum over y in Z^2, sum over c = 1..C^l  of  f_c(y) . H_n(k) psi_c^i(y - x)，其中的求和遍历所有空间位置 y 与输入通道 c。
多出来的颜色维度会成倍增加特征图数量，因此作者把每个滤波器分解为一个空间分量和一个逐点分量，把运算量与参数量的增长控制在色调旋转次数的一个小倍数以内。他们还提供了混合（hybrid）变体：只在 ResNet 早期、颜色选择性最强的阶段使用 CEConv，随后在颜色维度上做池化，在网络较深处引入颜色不变性，同时控制模型容量。
在不牺牲干净精度的前提下获得鲁棒性
最重要的结论是：颜色等变性几乎是「免费」地换来了在干净数据上的鲁棒性。在原始、未偏移的测试集上，CE-ResNet 与普通 ResNet 表现相当。差距只有在把测试图像按 -180 到 180 度逐步做色调偏移、并对整个范围取平均精度时才显现出来，而此时差距会急剧拉开。
图 2 用 Flowers-102 讲清了这个故事。先看普通 CNN（蓝线）：它在 0 度、也就是训练颜色所在处形成一个尖峰，色调一旦偏离就迅速跌到只有几个百分点。颜色等变模型（橙线）则出现三个峰，分别在 -120、0、120 度处，因为它的离散色调对称性让它在这几次旋转之后仍能认出同一朵花。再叠加 color-jitter 增强（橙色虚线），曲线会被抹平成在各个色调上都很高的精度。

zh.caption: 图 2 Flowers-102 上测试精度随测试时色调偏移的变化。普通 CNN（蓝线）只在训练颜色附近有峰值、其余处崩塌；颜色等变的 CE-CNN（橙线）在每一次离散色调旋转处都能恢复精度；再加上颜色增强（虚线）后，精度在整个色调范围内都保持在高位。

zh.text: 在整个色调扫描上取平均，Flowers-102 的精度从基线的 13.41% 提升到等变模型的 33.33%，大约是 2.5 倍，CIFAR-100 和 Stanford Cars 上也有相似幅度的提升。关键在于，这些鲁棒性收益并没有以干净精度为代价，而且它与颜色增强是叠加关系，而非彼此竞争。
一个受控压力测试：长尾 ColorMNIST
为了把机制单独拎出来，作者构造了一个合成基准——长尾 ColorMNIST：数字既要按形状、又要按颜色分类，且类别严重不均衡。由于颜色等变性会把一个形状模板共享到整个色谱，网络可以从常见颜色里学到某个数字的形状，再在罕见颜色下认出它——而这恰恰是普通网络样本用尽的地方。

zh.caption: 图 3 长尾 ColorMNIST 上的逐类别测试精度，灰色柱表示类别频率。颜色等变的 CECNN（绿线）即便在右侧的罕见类别上也能保持高精度，而普通 Z2CNN（蓝线）及其灰度变体（橙线）会随着类别变得稀少而急剧下滑。

zh.text: 这一效果相当显著。在所有类别上取平均，颜色等变网络达到 91.35%，而普通网络为 71.59%，提升了 19.76 个百分点，并且改进集中在最罕见、也正是参数共享意在拯救的那些类别上。这个受控实验印证了自然图像基准所暗示的结论：跨颜色共享形状，正是把罕见颜色样本从失败变为成功的关键。

zh.caption: 表 1 在完整的测试时色调扫描（-180 到 180 度）上的平均测试精度（%）。颜色等变 ResNet 远比普通基线鲁棒，同时在原始、未偏移的测试集上与之持平。

zh.text: 颜色等变性在什么时候有用？
颜色等变性并非万能，论文也坦诚地说明了它在什么情况下才划算。作者用一个颜色选择性（color selectivity）度量来量化一个数据集的神经元对颜色的响应程度，并把等变性的收益，与数据集的颜色选择性、以及等变阶段深入到网络多深，联系了起来。

zh.caption: 图 4 在不使用（左）和使用（右）color-jitter 增强的情况下，随着颜色等变性被嵌入到某一 ResNet 阶段为止，等变模型相对普通模型的精度提升。神经元高度颜色选择的 Flowers-102（颜色选择性 0.70）随等变性延伸到更深阶段而稳步获益；颜色选择性较弱的数据集则几乎没有提升。

zh.text: 规律很清楚：像 Flowers-102 这样颜色选择性很高的数据集（颜色选择性 0.70），把颜色等变性一直用到网络较深的阶段都能获益，而神经元不太在意颜色的数据集则几乎没有变化。另外两项消融进一步补全了设计图景。增加离散色调旋转的次数能提升测试时鲁棒性，但会略微牺牲容量，因为要保持参数量不变，通道数必须相应缩小。而群陪集池化（group coset pooling）正是带来色调不变性的机制；把它去掉，网络就退化得和普通网络一样。
共享滤波器到底学到了什么
由于等变性是被写进架构、而非从数据中学出来的，内部滤波器具有可解释的结构。对在 Flowers-102 上训练的 CE-ResNet18 做神经元特征可视化可以看到，一个共享滤波器的每一次旋转，都会响应同一个形状、只是渲染成不同的颜色——这正是参数共享被「看见」的样子。

zh.caption: 图 5 在 Flowers-102 上训练的 CE-ResNet18，其神经元特征及最强激活图块在四个阶段上的可视化。每个区块内，各行是同一个共享滤波器的不同色调旋转，每一行都在同一形状、不同颜色上激活，与颜色等变性的预言完全一致。

zh.text: 结论与边界
留下的核心信息是：颜色理应享有平移与旋转早已获得的那种等变待遇。通过在整个色谱上共享形状特征、同时把颜色保留在特征图的一个专用维度里，颜色等变卷积让网络得以同时做到「利用颜色」与「对颜色偏移鲁棒」，而不必二者取一。这一构件可以嵌入 ResNet 等现有架构，与颜色增强互补，并且恰好在它被设计去帮助的地方——颜色选择性强的数据集与出现不足的颜色——带来最大的收益。
诚实的边界在于，这份收益是有条件的。在神经元并不特别在意颜色的数据集上，等变性只是增加了参数却换不来多少提升；而多出来的颜色维度带来的计算开销，虽被滤波器分解压低，却并未消除。但只要用在颜色确实重要的地方，CEConv 就提供了一条干净、实用的通往颜色鲁棒识别的路径，也提醒我们：一个值得拥有的对称性，通常也值得直接内建进网络。
对实践者而言，它的吸引力还在于：这一切都不需要新的架构或新的训练流程。CEConv 可以直接替换标准卷积，参考实现也已开源，而混合变体让你能在计算预算与颜色等变的深度之间自由权衡。当任务依赖颜色、数据又无法覆盖所有外观时，它是一个在动用更重的不变性手段之前，值得优先一试、成本低廉的对称性。

en.subtitle: TU Delft's Color Equivariant Convolutions stay robust to test-time hue shifts without discarding color.

zh.text: 颜色是卷积神经网络最容易利用的线索之一：成熟的番茄是红的，校车是黄的，某种花有着独特的紫蓝色。网络很快就会学到这些规律，多数时候这也确实有帮助。但一旦测试时遇到的颜色与训练时不同，这种依赖就变成了软肋。一个主要从红色、银色样本里学到汽车的模型，看到一辆蓝色汽车时可能就认不出来了，哪怕形状一目了然。
对付这个问题的常规做法是追求颜色不变性（color invariance）：把图像转成灰度，或者用大量 color-jitter（颜色抖动）增强，直到网络不再在意色调。这样确实能换来鲁棒性，但代价很实在。灰度直接删掉了一个本来有用的信号，而强增强又会抹平区分类别所依赖的颜色差异。结果是，你恰恰通过拒绝使用颜色来获得对颜色的鲁棒性。

代尔夫特理工大学（TU Delft）计算机视觉实验室发表于 NeurIPS 2023 的一篇论文提出了另一种取舍。与其在「利用颜色」和「对颜色变化鲁棒」之间二选一，不如把一次色调偏移当作此前工作处理旋转或翻转那样的对象：把它视为网络理应在结构上遵守的一种对称性。承担这一职责的构件就是 Color Equivariant Convolution（CEConv，颜色等变卷积），它无需改动架构，就能作为标准模块直接嵌入 ResNet 这类现有骨干网络。

zh.caption: 图 1 核心思想。色调变换 T_g 把花 A 变成花 B。普通 CNN 会把两者映射到彼此无关的预测上，于是在一种颜色下学到的类别，换个颜色就可能认不出来。颜色等变网络（CECNN）则把它们映射到由一个可预测的置换 T'_g 相联系的表示上，因此为某种颜色学到的形状知识可以迁移到其他颜色。

zh.text: 论文地址：https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19368
代码地址：https://github.com/Attila94/CEConv

en.title: NeurIPS 2023 | Teaching CNNs to Treat Color as a Symmetry, Not a Shortcut
en.subtitle: TU Delft's Color Equivariant Convolutions stay robust to test-time hue shifts without discarding color.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让 CNN 把颜色当作一种对称性，而不是捷径
zh.subtitle: 代尔夫特理工大学提出 Color Equivariant Convolution（颜色等变卷积）：抵御测试时的色调偏移，又不丢弃颜色信息。

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea. A hue transform T_g turns flower A into flower B. A vanilla CNN maps the two into unrelated predictions, so a class it learned in one color may be unrecognizable in another. A Color Equivariant CNN (CECNN) instead maps them to representations related by a predictable permutation T'_g, so shape knowledge learned for one color transfers to the others.

en.text: The problem: color helps, until the colors change

Real-world appearance has a long tail. For almost any object category, some colors are common in the training set and others are rare or entirely absent, and no realistic dataset can cover every variation. Because a standard CNN treats each color as its own visual pattern, the shape knowledge it builds for a well-represented color does not automatically carry over to an underrepresented one. The rare colors are exactly the ones that get misclassified, and collecting a perfectly color-balanced dataset is not a practical option.

The paper first makes the tension concrete: CNNs clearly benefit from color, yet they are not robust to color-based distribution shifts. Grayscale models and color augmentation restore robustness, but they do so by discarding the discriminative color information that helps in the first place. The goal is to keep color and generalize across it at the same time, so that a shape learned in one part of the spectrum is available everywhere.

zh.caption: 图 1 核心思想。色调变换 T_g 把花 A 变成花 B。普通 CNN 会把两者映射到彼此无关的预测上，于是在一种颜色下学到的类别，换个颜色就可能认不出来。颜色等变网络（CECNN）则把它们映射到由一个可预测的置换 T'_g 相联系的表示上，因此为某种颜色学到的形状知识可以迁移到其他颜色。

zh.text: 问题：颜色有用，直到颜色变了
真实世界的外观有一条长尾。对几乎任何一个物体类别来说，训练集中总有些颜色常见、另一些颜色罕见甚至完全缺席，任何现实数据集都无法覆盖全部变化。由于标准 CNN 把每一种颜色都当作独立的视觉模式，它为某种充分出现的颜色所建立的形状知识，并不会自动迁移到出现不足的颜色上。恰恰是那些罕见颜色最容易被错分，而收集一个颜色完全均衡的数据集在实践中并不可行。
论文首先把这层张力讲清楚：CNN 明显能从颜色中获益，却对基于颜色的分布偏移并不鲁棒。灰度模型和颜色增强能恢复鲁棒性，但代价是丢弃了原本有用的判别性颜色信息。目标是既保留颜色、又能跨颜色泛化，让在色谱某一段学到的形状，在整个色谱上都能用得上。

en.subtitle: TU Delft's Color Equivariant Convolutions stay robust to test-time hue shifts without discarding color.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让 CNN 把颜色当作一种对称性，而不是捷径
zh.subtitle: 代尔夫特理工大学提出 Color Equivariant Convolution（颜色等变卷积）：抵御测试时的色调偏移，又不丢弃颜色信息。

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea. A hue transform T_g turns flower A into flower B. A vanilla CNN maps the two into unrelated predictions, so a class it learned in one color may be unrecognizable in another. A Color Equivariant CNN (CECNN) instead maps them to representations related by a predictable permutation T'_g, so shape knowledge learned for one color transfers to the others.

en.text: The idea: a hue shift is a rotation in RGB space

Group equivariant convolutions taught networks to share parameters across geometric transformations such as rotations and reflections, which made them far more data efficient for those symmetries. Photometric transformations like hue shifts had been left out, even though studies of trained CNNs show that early layers learn strongly color-selective filters. Color, in other words, is a natural axis along which to demand equivariance.

The key observation is geometric. A hue shift in HSV space corresponds, in RGB space, to a rotation around the gray diagonal that runs from black to white, the [1,1,1] axis. The authors formalize the set of discrete hue shifts as the group H_n of n rotations by 360/n degrees about that diagonal. A Color Equivariant Convolution then correlates the input not with a single filter but with a set of hue-rotated copies of it, producing a feature map that carries an extra dimension indexing which hue rotation each response came from.

For the input layer this means rotating each filter by the hue matrix H_n(k); for hidden layers the filter copies are cyclically permuted across the color dimension, so equivariance is preserved all the way through the network. Concretely, the response at spatial location x and hue index k is:
[f * psi^i](x, k) = sum over y in Z^2, sum over c = 1..C^l  of  f_c(y) . H_n(k) psi_c^i(y - x), where the sum runs over spatial positions y and input channels c.

The extra color dimension multiplies the number of feature maps, so the authors keep the cost in check by decomposing each filter into a spatial and a pointwise component, which limits the growth in operations and parameters to a small factor of the number of hue rotations. They also offer hybrid variants that apply CEConvs only in the early, most color-selective ResNet stages and then pool over the color dimension, introducing color invariance later in the network while controlling capacity.

zh.caption: 图 1 核心思想。色调变换 T_g 把花 A 变成花 B。普通 CNN 会把两者映射到彼此无关的预测上，于是在一种颜色下学到的类别，换个颜色就可能认不出来。颜色等变网络（CECNN）则把它们映射到由一个可预测的置换 T'_g 相联系的表示上，因此为某种颜色学到的形状知识可以迁移到其他颜色。

zh.text: 思路：色调偏移就是 RGB 空间里的一次旋转
群等变卷积（group equivariant convolution）教会网络在旋转、反射等几何变换间共享参数，从而在这些对称性上大幅提升数据效率。而像色调偏移这样的光度变换却一直被搁置，尽管对已训练 CNN 的研究表明，早期层会学到高度颜色选择性的滤波器。换句话说，颜色本身就是一个天然适合施加等变性的坐标轴。
关键的观察是几何性的。HSV 空间中的一次色调偏移，对应到 RGB 空间就是绕着从黑到白的灰度对角线（即 [1,1,1] 轴）的一次旋转。作者把离散色调偏移的集合形式化为群 H_n，即绕该对角线做 n 次、每次 360/n 度旋转所构成的群。颜色等变卷积于是不再只用单个滤波器与输入做相关，而是用一组经过色调旋转的滤波器副本，产生的特征图会多出一个维度，用来标记每个响应来自哪一次色调旋转。
对于输入层，这意味着用色调矩阵 H_n(k) 旋转每个滤波器；对于隐藏层，滤波器副本沿颜色维度做循环置换，从而让等变性在整个网络中一直保持。具体地，空间位置 x、色调索引 k 处的响应为：
[f * psi^i](x, k) = sum over y in Z^2, sum over c = 1..C^l  of  f_c(y) . H_n(k) psi_c^i(y - x)，其中的求和遍历所有空间位置 y 与输入通道 c。
多出来的颜色维度会成倍增加特征图数量，因此作者把每个滤波器分解为一个空间分量和一个逐点分量，把运算量与参数量的增长控制在色调旋转次数的一个小倍数以内。他们还提供了混合（hybrid）变体：只在 ResNet 早期、颜色选择性最强的阶段使用 CEConv，随后在颜色维度上做池化，在网络较深处引入颜色不变性，同时控制模型容量。

zh.subtitle: 代尔夫特理工大学提出 Color Equivariant Convolution（颜色等变卷积）：抵御测试时的色调偏移，又不丢弃颜色信息。

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea. A hue transform T_g turns flower A into flower B. A vanilla CNN maps the two into unrelated predictions, so a class it learned in one color may be unrecognizable in another. Takeaways and limits

The lasting message is that color deserves the same equivariance treatment that translation and rotation have long enjoyed. By sharing shape features across the color spectrum while keeping color in a dedicated dimension of the feature map, Color Equivariant Convolutions let a network exploit color and stay robust to color shifts at once, rather than trading one for the other. The block plugs into existing architectures like ResNet, complements color augmentation, and delivers its largest gains precisely on the color-selective datasets and underrepresented colors where it is designed to help.

The honest boundary is that the benefit is conditional. On datasets whose neurons are not especially color-selective, equivariance adds parameters without buying much, and the extra color dimension carries a compute overhead that the filter decomposition reduces but does not erase. Used where color genuinely matters, though, CEConvs offer a clean, practical route to color-robust recognition, and a reminder that a symmetry worth having is usually worth building in.

For practitioners, part of the appeal is that none of this asks for a new architecture or a new training recipe. A CEConv is a drop-in replacement for a standard convolution, the reference implementation is public, and the hybrid variants let you trade the depth of color equivariance against your compute budget. When a task leans on color and the data cannot cover every appearance, it is a cheap symmetry to try before reaching for heavier invariance machinery.

zh.text: 在不牺牲干净精度的前提下获得鲁棒性
最重要的结论是：颜色等变性几乎是「免费」地换来了在干净数据上的鲁棒性。在原始、未偏移的测试集上，CE-ResNet 与普通 ResNet 表现相当。差距只有在把测试图像按 -180 到 180 度逐步做色调偏移、并对整个范围取平均精度时才显现出来，而此时差距会急剧拉开。
图 2 用 Flowers-102 讲清了这个故事。先看普通 CNN（蓝线）：它在 0 度、也就是训练颜色所在处形成一个尖峰，色调一旦偏离就迅速跌到只有几个百分点。颜色等变模型（橙线）则出现三个峰，分别在 -120、0、120 度处，因为它的离散色调对称性让它在这几次旋转之后仍能认出同一朵花。再叠加 color-jitter 增强（橙色虚线），曲线会被抹平成在各个色调上都很高的精度。

zh.caption: 图 2 Flowers-102 上测试精度随测试时色调偏移的变化。普通 CNN（蓝线）只在训练颜色附近有峰值、其余处崩塌；颜色等变的 CE-CNN（橙线）在每一次离散色调旋转处都能恢复精度；再加上颜色增强（虚线）后，精度在整个色调范围内都保持在高位。

zh.text: 在整个色调扫描上取平均，Flowers-102 的精度从基线的 13.41% 提升到等变模型的 33.33%，大约是 2.5 倍，CIFAR-100 和 Stanford Cars 上也有相似幅度的提升。关键在于，这些鲁棒性收益并没有以干净精度为代价，而且它与颜色增强是叠加关系，而非彼此竞争。

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让 CNN 把颜色当作一种对称性，而不是捷径

en.text: A controlled stress test: long-tailed ColorMNIST

To isolate the mechanism, the authors build a synthetic benchmark, long-tailed ColorMNIST, where digits must be classified by both shape and color and the classes are strongly imbalanced. Because color equivariance shares a shape template across the whole color spectrum, a network can learn a digit's shape from the common colors and still recognize it in the rare ones, which is precisely where a vanilla network runs out of examples.

en.caption: Figure 3. Per-class test accuracy on long-tailed ColorMNIST, with the gray bars showing class frequency. The color equivariant CECNN (green) holds high accuracy even for the rare classes on the right, while the vanilla Z2CNN (blue) and its grayscale variant (orange) fall off sharply as classes become infrequent.

en.text: The effect is large. Averaged over all classes, the color equivariant network reaches 91.35% against the vanilla network's 71.59%, a gain of 19.76 points, and the improvement is concentrated exactly on the rarest classes that parameter sharing is meant to rescue. The controlled setting confirms what the natural-image benchmarks suggest: sharing shape across colors is what turns rare-color examples from failures into successes.

en.caption: Table 1. Average test accuracy (%) over the full test-time hue-shift sweep (-180 to 180 degrees). Color equivariant ResNets are far more robust than vanilla baselines, while matching them on the original, unshifted test sets.

zh.text: 一个受控压力测试：长尾 ColorMNIST
为了把机制单独拎出来，作者构造了一个合成基准——长尾 ColorMNIST：数字既要按形状、又要按颜色分类，且类别严重不均衡。由于颜色等变性会把一个形状模板共享到整个色谱，网络可以从常见颜色里学到某个数字的形状，再在罕见颜色下认出它——而这恰恰是普通网络样本用尽的地方。

zh.caption: 图 3 长尾 ColorMNIST 上的逐类别测试精度，灰色柱表示类别频率。颜色等变的 CECNN（绿线）即便在右侧的罕见类别上也能保持高精度，而普通 Z2CNN（蓝线）及其灰度变体（橙线）会随着类别变得稀少而急剧下滑。

zh.text: 这一效果相当显著。在所有类别上取平均，颜色等变网络达到 91.35%，而普通网络为 71.59%，提升了 19.76 个百分点，并且改进集中在最罕见、也正是参数共享意在拯救的那些类别上。这个受控实验印证了自然图像基准所暗示的结论：跨颜色共享形状，正是把罕见颜色样本从失败变为成功的关键。

zh.caption: 表 1 在完整的测试时色调扫描（-180 到 180 度）上的平均测试精度（%）。颜色等变 ResNet 远比普通基线鲁棒，同时在原始、未偏移的测试集上与之持平。

对付这个问题的常规做法是追求颜色不变性（color invariance）：把图像转成灰度，或者用大量 color-jitter（颜色抖动）增强，直到网络不再在意色调。这样确实能换来鲁棒性，但代价很实在。灰度直接删掉了一个本来有用的信号，而强增强又会抹平区分类别所依赖的颜色差异。结果是，你恰恰通过拒绝使用颜色来获得对颜色的鲁棒性。

代尔夫特理工大学（TU Delft）计算机视觉实验室发表于 NeurIPS 2023 的一篇论文提出了另一种取舍。与其在「利用颜色」和「对颜色变化鲁棒」之间二选一，不如把一次色调偏移当作此前工作处理旋转或翻转那样的对象：把它视为网络理应在结构上遵守的一种对称性。承担这一职责的构件就是 Color Equivariant Convolution（CEConv，颜色等变卷积），它无需改动架构，就能作为标准模块直接嵌入 ResNet 这类现有骨干网络。

zh.caption: 图 1 核心思想。色调变换 T_g 把花 A 变成花 B。普通 CNN 会把两者映射到彼此无关的预测上，于是在一种颜色下学到的类别，换个颜色就可能认不出来。颜色等变网络（CECNN）则把它们映射到由一个可预测的置换 T'_g 相联系的表示上，因此为某种颜色学到的形状知识可以迁移到其他颜色。

zh.text: 论文地址：https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19368
代码地址：https://github.com/Attila94/CEConv
在不牺牲干净精度的前提下获得鲁棒性
最重要的结论是：颜色等变性几乎是「免费」地换来了在干净数据上的鲁棒性。在原始、未偏移的测试集上，CE-ResNet 与普通 ResNet 表现相当。差距只有在把测试图像按 -180 到 180 度逐步做色调偏移、并对整个范围取平均精度时才显现出来，而此时差距会急剧拉开。
图 2 用 Flowers-102 讲清了这个故事。先看普通 CNN（蓝线）：它在 0 度、也就是训练颜色所在处形成一个尖峰，色调一旦偏离就迅速跌到只有几个百分点。颜色等变模型（橙线）则出现三个峰，分别在 -120、0、120 度处，因为它的离散色调对称性让它在这几次旋转之后仍能认出同一朵花。再叠加 color-jitter 增强（橙色虚线），曲线会被抹平成在各个色调上都很高的精度。

zh.caption: 图 2 Flowers-102 上测试精度随测试时色调偏移的变化。普通 CNN（蓝线）只在训练颜色附近有峰值、其余处崩塌；颜色等变的 CE-CNN（橙线）在每一次离散色调旋转处都能恢复精度；再加上颜色增强（虚线）后，精度在整个色调范围内都保持在高位。

zh.text: 在整个色调扫描上取平均，Flowers-102 的精度从基线的 13.41% 提升到等变模型的 33.33%，大约是 2.5 倍，CIFAR-100 和 Stanford Cars 上也有相似幅度的提升。关键在于，这些鲁棒性收益并没有以干净精度为代价，而且它与颜色增强是叠加关系，而非彼此竞争。

en.title: NeurIPS 2023 | Teaching CNNs to Treat Color as a Symmetry, Not a Shortcut
en.subtitle: TU Delft's Color Equivariant Convolutions stay robust to test-time hue shifts without discarding color.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让 CNN 把颜色当作一种对称性，而不是捷径
zh.subtitle: 代尔夫特理工大学提出 Color Equivariant Convolution（颜色等变卷积）：抵御测试时的色调偏移，又不丢弃颜色信息。

en.text: Color is one of the most reliable cues a convolutional network can lean on. A ripe tomato is red, a school bus is yellow, a particular flower is a characteristic purple-blue. Networks pick up on this quickly, and most of the time it helps. But the same reliance becomes a liability the moment the colors at test time drift away from the colors seen during training. A model that learned cars mostly from red and silver examples can stumble on a blue one, even though the shape is unmistakable.

The usual defense against this is color invariance: convert to grayscale, or drown the network in aggressive color-jitter augmentation until it stops caring about hue. That does buy robustness, but at a real cost. Grayscale simply deletes a genuinely useful signal, and heavy augmentation blurs the very color distinctions that separate one class from another. You end up robust to color precisely by refusing to use it.

A NeurIPS 2023 paper from the Computer Vision Lab at Delft University of Technology proposes a different bargain. Instead of choosing between exploiting color and being robust to color changes, it treats a hue shift the way earlier work treated a rotation or a flip: as a symmetry the network should respect by construction. The building block that does this is the Color Equivariant Convolution (CEConv), and it drops into a standard ResNet with no architectural surgery.

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea. A hue transform T_g turns flower A into flower B. A vanilla CNN maps the two into unrelated predictions, so a class it learned in one color may be unrecognizable in another. A Color Equivariant CNN (CECNN) instead maps them to representations related by a predictable permutation T'_g, so shape knowledge learned for one color transfers to the others.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.19368
Code: https://github.com/Attila94/CEConv

zh.text: 颜色等变性在什么时候有用？
颜色等变性并非万能，论文也坦诚地说明了它在什么情况下才划算。作者用一个颜色选择性（color selectivity）度量来量化一个数据集的神经元对颜色的响应程度，并把等变性的收益，与数据集的颜色选择性、以及等变阶段深入到网络多深，联系了起来。

zh.caption: 图 4 在不使用（左）和使用（右）color-jitter 增强的情况下，随着颜色等变性被嵌入到某一 ResNet 阶段为止，等变模型相对普通模型的精度提升。神经元高度颜色选择的 Flowers-102（颜色选择性 0.70）随等变性延伸到更深阶段而稳步获益；颜色选择性较弱的数据集则几乎没有提升。

zh.text: 规律很清楚：像 Flowers-102 这样颜色选择性很高的数据集（颜色选择性 0.70），把颜色等变性一直用到网络较深的阶段都能获益，而神经元不太在意颜色的数据集则几乎没有变化。另外两项消融进一步补全了设计图景。增加离散色调旋转的次数能提升测试时鲁棒性，但会略微牺牲容量，因为要保持参数量不变，通道数必须相应缩小。而群陪集池化（group coset pooling）正是带来色调不变性的机制；把它去掉，网络就退化得和普通网络一样。

Code: https://github.com/Attila94/CEConv

zh.text: 一个受控压力测试：长尾 ColorMNIST
为了把机制单独拎出来，作者构造了一个合成基准——长尾 ColorMNIST：数字既要按形状、又要按颜色分类，且类别严重不均衡。由于颜色等变性会把一个形状模板共享到整个色谱，网络可以从常见颜色里学到某个数字的形状，再在罕见颜色下认出它——而这恰恰是普通网络样本用尽的地方。

zh.caption: 图 3 长尾 ColorMNIST 上的逐类别测试精度，灰色柱表示类别频率。颜色等变的 CECNN（绿线）即便在右侧的罕见类别上也能保持高精度，而普通 Z2CNN（蓝线）及其灰度变体（橙线）会随着类别变得稀少而急剧下滑。

zh.text: 这一效果相当显著。在所有类别上取平均，颜色等变网络达到 91.35%，而普通网络为 71.59%，提升了 19.76 个百分点，并且改进集中在最罕见、也正是参数共享意在拯救的那些类别上。这个受控实验印证了自然图像基准所暗示的结论：跨颜色共享形状，正是把罕见颜色样本从失败变为成功的关键。

zh.caption: 表 1 在完整的测试时色调扫描（-180 到 180 度）上的平均测试精度（%）。颜色等变 ResNet 远比普通基线鲁棒，同时在原始、未偏移的测试集上与之持平。

en.subtitle: TU Delft's Color Equivariant Convolutions stay robust to test-time hue shifts without discarding color.

zh.title: NeurIPS 2023 | 让 CNN 把颜色当作一种对称性，而不是捷径
zh.subtitle: 代尔夫特理工大学提出 Color Equivariant Convolution（颜色等变卷积）：抵御测试时的色调偏移，又不丢弃颜色信息。

en.caption: Figure 1. The core idea. A hue transform T_g turns flower A into flower B. A vanilla CNN maps the two into unrelated predictions, so a class it learned in one color may be unrecognizable in another. A Color Equivariant CNN (CECNN) instead maps them to representations related by a predictable permutation T'_g, so shape knowledge learned for one color transfers to the others.

en.text: Takeaways and limits

The lasting message is that color deserves the same equivariance treatment that translation and rotation have long enjoyed. By sharing shape features across the color spectrum while keeping color in a dedicated dimension of the feature map, Color Equivariant Convolutions let a network exploit color and stay robust to color shifts at once, rather than trading one for the other. The block plugs into existing architectures like ResNet, complements color augmentation, and delivers its largest gains precisely on the color-selective datasets and underrepresented colors where it is designed to help.

The honest boundary is that the benefit is conditional. On datasets whose neurons are not especially color-selective, equivariance adds parameters without buying much, and the extra color dimension carries a compute overhead that the filter decomposition reduces but does not erase. Used where color genuinely matters, though, CEConvs offer a clean, practical route to color-robust recognition, and a reminder that a symmetry worth having is usually worth building in.

For practitioners, part of the appeal is that none of this asks for a new architecture or a new training recipe. A CEConv is a drop-in replacement for a standard convolution, the reference implementation is public, and the hybrid variants let you trade the depth of color equivariance against your compute budget. When a task leans on color and the data cannot cover every appearance, it is a cheap symmetry to try before reaching for heavier invariance machinery.
